clue.text: Not altogether courteous, almost icy, nothing but a party type

indicators.note: not altogether says the word for courteous loses its final letter here

parts.note: courteous means polite

indicators.note: almost says the word icy stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A person described as a bit rude and nearly frosty, nothing but a party animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not altogether' trims POLITE to POLIT; 'almost' trims ICY to IC; add O for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a politician or political activist, someone who is a party person in the political sense.

clue.text: Underwear that's left to hang about

indicators.note: left means gone away, so these letters depart from the underwear word

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear
i.e. stands for 'that is', so that's gives IE

explanation.surface: Some underwear abandoned and left dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' tells you IE (i.e., 'that is') has gone from LINGERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay around or dawdle, a synonym of hang about.

clue.text: One uses sleight of hand to deceive one in box

parts.note: to con someone is to deceive them
a juror sits in the jury box

explanation.surface: A magician uses dexterity to trick someone in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is the jury box, not a magician's cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror is a magician who performs tricks by nimble handwork.

clue.text: Conveyance said to be generous

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: handsome can mean generous, as in a handsome donation

explanation.surface: A vehicle reputed to be lavish.
explanation.walkthrough: A HANSOM is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab of Victorian London.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom cab is a horse-drawn carriage, a means of transport or conveyance.

clue.text: Benefit favouring the healthy

parts.note: pro means in favour of
fit means healthy

explanation.surface: An advantage that goes to people in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is gain or advantage, a synonym of benefit as a noun.

clue.text: Introduction to a stiffly formal ruler?

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, a ruler

explanation.surface: A guide to a very strait-laced measuring stick, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruler is a monarch, ER, not a measuring stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is an elementary textbook giving an introduction to a subject.

clue.text: Murphy takes a shot at nothing

parts.note: a pot is a shot, as at snooker or a pot shot
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone called Murphy has a go at an empty target.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is informal (originally Irish) slang for a potato, so the man's name is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy is a slang term for a potato, from the Irish surname.

clue.text: Person secures zero return using a computer

indicators.note: secures means holds firmly within, so one word wraps round another

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

indicators.note: return says the word for zero is read backwards

parts.note: nil means zero

explanation.surface: Someone guarantees no comeback while at a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person' gives ONE in the impersonal sense ('one never knows'), not a named individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Being online means being connected to the internet, working by computer.

clue.text: Latest thing in London topiary?

definitions.meaning: the most advanced point of a development
said with a dropped H in a London accent, hedge-trimming sounds like this phrase

explanation.surface: The trendiest thing in shaping bushes in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney Londoners traditionally drop their H's, so 'hedge' becomes 'edge'; topiary is cutting hedges into shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting edge means the forefront of progress, the newest and most advanced development.

clue.text: Flier over Iran may help to get 7

indicators.note: over means covering, so the flier word spreads over and around the other piece

parts.note: a wing is what flies, or an RAF unit of fliers
IR is the international abbreviation for Iran

explanation.surface: An aircraft passing over Iran could help someone get connected.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is 7-down; wiring helps a computer get on the network.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical and network wiring connects a computer, helping it go on the internet.

clue.text: July nuts cracked with criminal intent

indicators.note: cracked means broken open, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Summer nuts broken open by a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjustly means wrongfully or unfairly, acting with wrongful purpose.

clue.text: Source of exotic food sounds capital

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard rather than spelt, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Delhi, as New Delhi, is the capital of India

explanation.surface: Somewhere supplying foreign food that sounds excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like the adjective meaning excellent; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli or delicatessen sells imported and unusual prepared foods.

clue.text: Backing for old age

definitions.meaning: retiring is withdrawing or moving back, so this is backing away
the period after leaving work in later life

explanation.definitionFit: Retirement means withdrawal or retreat, and also the stage of life after work ends.

clue.text: Lodge broken contract once emanating from Victoria

indicators.note: broken means smashed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to contract is to narrow

explanation.surface: A lodge breaks an agreement that previously came from the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Golden Arrow was a luxury boat train that ran from London's Victoria station to Dover for Paris, until 1972.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Arrow was a train service which used to depart from Victoria station.

clue.text: Awkward mound due to something in the middle

indicators.note: awkward means ungainly or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy heap due to something central.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine, in the middle of the body.

clue.text: Mail pony beaten by athlete

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A postal pony outrun by a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An Olympian is a competitor at the Olympic Games, an athlete.

clue.text: Vehicle with one in pursuit

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one within the pursuit word

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A carriage with somebody chasing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise is a light horse-drawn carriage, a vehicle.

clue.text: Free place given precedence, which is rotten

indicators.note: given precedence means placed first, so the place word comes before the free word

parts.note: to put is to place
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A vacant spot is put first, and it stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given precedence' puts PUT ahead of RID even though 'Free' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrid means decaying and foul, rotten.

clue.text: Acclamation over a tumult, such as Ben Hur

indicators.note: over means covering, so the acclamation word spreads round the other pieces

parts.note: a cheer is acclamation
a riot is a tumult

explanation.surface: Applause above an uproar, the sort a famous film epic gets.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben-Hur is the hero of the novel and film famed for its chariot race.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben-Hur drove a chariot in the famous race, so he exemplifies a chariot driver.

clue.text: Spots hesitation with less careful cut

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Pimples and a pause from a more reckless slice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works two ways: more rash, and a slice of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a slice of bacon, and rasher also means more reckless or less careful.

clue.text: Plant makes radio almost quiet

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word radio, dropping its last letter

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A factory produces a nearly silent wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory; it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a plant grown for its edible pungent root.

clue.text: Reader's possessive

parts.note: the possessive word that belongs to the reader being addressed, as in 'this book is ...'

explanation.definitionFit: The possessive adjective for 'you' indicates belonging to whoever is reading or listening.

clue.text: Spirits for composer and poet

parts.note: gins are spirits
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: Drinks for a musician and a writer of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Allen Ginsberg was an American Beat poet, author of Howl.

clue.text: Leave record in river

indicators.note: in places the record inside the river

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Drop a disc in the water and go.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave or go away.

clue.text: Sight and sound of a monumental building

indicators.note: sound of says the word is heard rather than spelt, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the Eiffel Tower in Paris is a monumental structure

explanation.surface: Seeing and hearing an impressive edifice.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is a good look at something, a striking sight.

clue.text: Foulness, say, is light

parts.note: taken as written
to light is to land, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A dirty quality might be bright.
explanation.walkthrough: Foulness looks like a noun for dirtiness; it is Foulness Island off the Essex coast in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Foulness is an island in Essex, an example of an island, signalled by 'say'.
